newsitem.title: JAPAN: Thailand, Japan to cooperate on currencies--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Thailand, Japan to cooperate on currencies--MOF.

text.p: Thailand and Japan have agreed to cooperate to promote stability in the currency markets, and cooperative measures could include intervention, a senior official from Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Friday.
The official briefed reporters following a meeting between Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka.
The meeting was also attended by Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond, he said.
"Finance Minister Mitsuzuka and Thai Finance Minister Thanong agreed that we will cooperate closely in the markets for a stable baht. This includes intervention for the baht," the official said.
Asked if any concrete measures for currency cooperation, such as the use of a repo pact, were discussed during the meeting, the official declined to comment.
"There was no request from the Thai side for financial support," he added.
Thailand was not asking for any financial support from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) or the Export-Import Bank of Japan, the official said.
"Thailand is asking for technical assistance from the IMF, as it had been before. It is not asking for financial support from the IMF," the official said.
There were no discussions about support from Japanese banks, either, he added.
Asked whether the Thais called on Japan to join an international support scheme in the future should a need arise for one, the official said the issue was not discussed.
Most of the 40-minute talk was dominated by Thailand explaining its move towards a managed floating system for the baht and financial and fiscal steps taken for the economy, the official said.
Both the Thai finance minister and the central bank governor said those measures will help Thai economic growth, he said.

Mitsuzuka was quoted as telling the Thai officials that the steps taken were timely and appropriate. MOF minister also told them that he believed that the Thai authorities will be successful in bringing the matter under control, he said.
Asked whether Thailand explained about their foreign reserves, the official said the topic was not discussed.
Thailand did not explain to the Japanese side their economic outlook, he added.
